stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5NXJ7 While most internet connections are down, pictures of tanks in the city of Alamata are in circulation Image: Social Media/REUTERS Advertisement Over the past week, three militias from a new alliance, led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) , have been fighting the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) in northern Ethiopia . The heterogeneous alliance that calls itself the "Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival" brings together seven armed domestic groups that oppose Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's federal government. However, the ENDF has painted a picture of an alliance that extends far beyond Ethiopia's borders: Its commander-in-chief, Field Marshal Birhanu Jula, accused Eritrea , Sudan and Egypt of supporting the TPLF. Sudan dismissed the allegation as "baseless." Its military government countered with accusations that Ethiopia was supporting the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia that has been fighting Sudan's army for over three years . Eritrea said Ethiopia was attempting to shift responsibility for its own internal conflicts onto its neighbors.

stories.summary: Ethiopia: Overnight Explosions Reported in Addis Abeba Amid Northern Ethiopia Fighting Seyoum Getu / Deutsche Welle Ethiopian army special forces and militia fighting in the Afar region. 1 October 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — Explosions were heard in Ethiopia's capital shortly after midnight on Thursday, with diplomatic sources reporting blasts near the Ethiopian National Defense Forces (ENDF) headquarters and another military installation, as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises concerns that the conflict could spread to the capital. Three diplomatic sources told Reuters that explosions were heard overnight in Addis Abeba. A source linked to the opposition alliance fighting federal forces in northern Ethiopia since last week told Reuters that the alliance had carried out several drone strikes in the capital, including against military facilities. Reuters said it could not independently verify the claim. A diplomatic source who informed Addis Standard said explosions were reported at about 12:30 a.m. and 1:15 a.m. local time, including in areas near the ENDF headquarters and the site believed to house the Meshualekia 4th Division.

stories.title: Mauritius: Mauritius Rights Body Calls for Marriage Equality
stories.summary: Mauritius Rights Body Calls for Marriage Equality 1 October 2026 Human Rights Watch (Washington, DC) By Ryan Thoreson Lawmakers Should Act to Codify Protections The National Human Rights Commission in Mauritius earlier this year urged the government to legally recognize same-sex marriages, stating that the refusal to recognize such unions is discriminatory and lacks justification under domestic law. The Commission's recommendation comes after two same-sex couples filed complaints alleging that the country's civil status office's refusal to register their marriage is prejudicial to them. In their complaints and in public testimony before the Commission, same-sex couples and lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) individuals testified about the burdens they face with regard to taxation, inheritance, immigration, medical decision-making, family formation, and social acceptance in the absence of partnership recognition. The Commission agreed that any exclusion of same-sex couples from marriage could amount to discrimination and recommended the formation of a government committee to eliminate discrimination in partnership recognition and marriage. Amira Osman, head of the No to the Oppression of Women initiative , told Radio Dabanga that a young woman who fled the Murda neighbourhood in Omdurman with her mother was repeatedly gang-raped during their journey in search of dialysis treatment. The General Coordination for Displaced Persons and Refugees in Darfur has documented more than 100 cases of malnutrition among children in the Soni area of East Jebel Marra, along with at least 30 deaths linked to complications from malnutrition and a lack of healthcare. The court , originally set up to handle economic matters related to the Ecowas Treaty, was given a human rights mandate in 2005. Since then, of the hundreds of cases the court has heard, nearly 90% have been human rights-related. In a recent book, international law and human rights scholar Maame Efua Addadzi-Koom argues that the shift in the court's mandate has made it an accessible forum for advancing women's rights. Alan joined the university in 1972, but left after a couple of years to teach in Britain at Cambridge University, and then in the US at NorthEastern University in Chicago. However, Kenya had got a hold on him, and he returned to work there, first for Amref , a Dutch organisation, and then GTZ, a German body, mainly in family planning and public health. Eventually he went freelance, helping various aid agencies with their work in Kenya, until a serious accident incapacitated him, forcing him to retire to Scotland. Born in Glasgow , Alan was the son of Bill, an analytical chemist, and Jessie (nee Moncrieff), a shorthand typist.

stories.title: RDC-France : de Kinshasa à Bunia, les enjeux de la visite de Jean-Noël Barrot
stories.summary: Le ministre français des Affaires étrangères se rend les 2 et 3 octobre en RDC, avant une conférence humanitaire à Paris. Il fera une étape, inédite pour le chef de la diplomatie française, dans l’est du pays.

stories.title: Pourquoi l’Algérie a élargi la peine de mort aux incendiaires et aux kidnappeurs d’enfants
stories.summary: Après les feux de forêts intenses et meurtriers de l’été, le chef de l’Etat, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a souhaité élargir le nombre de « crimes capitaux », passibles de la peine de mort. Le pays respectait pourtant un moratoire sur cette question depuis 1993.

stories.title: Cameroun : pourquoi Vision 4, la chaîne de télévision d’Amougou Belinga, a été suspendue
stories.summary: Incarcéré depuis deux ans dans le cadre de l’affaire Martinez Zogo, du nom du journaliste tué à Yaoundé en 2023, Jean-Pierre Amougou Belinga voit sa chaîne de télévision privée d’antenne pour un mois par le Conseil national de la communication. Un nouveau bras de fer s’engage donc avec le régulateur.

stories.title: Nigerian Charged With Running Fake Government Agency
stories.summary: The Nigerian secured office space in a federal building, opened bank accounts and even held meetings with foreign diplomats. He says he is innocent.

stories.title: L'AfCRA, une agence de notation africaine pour contrer les biais des géants mondiaux
stories.summary: Publicité L'AfCRA, une agence de notation africaine pour contrer les biais des géants mondiaux Analyse Afrique Le continent africain s'apprête à inaugurer sa propre agence de notation de crédit. Développée en collaboration avec l'Union Africaine, l'AfCRA compte fournir une évaluation du risque de crédit adaptée aux réalités africaines, face à des agences internationales régulièrement accusées de sévérité excessive envers l'Afrique. Publié le : 01/10/2026 - 19:50 4 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : David Rich L'Agence africaine de notation de crédit (AfCRA) ambitionne d'offrir une évaluation du risque de crédit plus équitable que les grandes agences de notation. © studio graphique FMM Moody's, Fitch, S&P... et maintenant l'AfCRA. L'Agence africaine de notation de crédit, spécifique au continent, sera inaugurée le 7 octobre à Port-Louis, capitale de l'Ile Maurice, où se trouve son siège. Développée par l' Union africaine mais conçue comme une institution indépendante, l'AfCRA a pour but d'offrir une évaluation du risque de crédit mieux adaptée aux réalités africaines et de faciliter l'accès à l'emprunt sur les marchés internationaux, qui demeure très difficile et cher pour un grand nombre de pays du continent.

stories.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 2, 2026
stories.summary: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 2, 2026 AllAfrica AllAfrica logo 2 October 2026 allAfrica.com By Melody Chironda Ethiopia, Eritrea Cut Diplomatic Ties as Conflict Escalates Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises fears of a wider regional conflict. Ethiopia announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats, accusing them of posing a national security threat, prompting Eritrea to respond by cutting ties. The move follows worsening tensions over allegations that Eritrea is supporting armed groups fighting the Ethiopian government, which Asmara denies, as well as disagreements over Ethiopia's push for access to the Red Sea. Fighting between Ethiopian forces, the Tigray People's Liberation Front and allied groups has intensified across Tigray, Afar and Amhara. The African Union and United Nations have urged restraint and warned of growing risks to civilians and humanitarian operations.

stories.title: East African countries are racing to finish preparations ahead of AFCON 2027
stories.summary: With less than nine months to go before the start of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, host nations Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are scrambling to finish preparations amid rumours of a potential relocation.

stories.title: Algeria introduces death penalty for arsonists after deadly wildfires
stories.summary: Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images By Doug Faulkner Published 1 October 2026 Algeria has adopted a law imposing the death penalty on people convicted of arson of forests or fields after a series of deadly wildfires swept parts of the country. Members of the national assembly voted through the bill, which also made child abduction a capital offence, on Thursday. Capital punishment has been in the country's penal code for some offences, but no execution has been carried out since 1993. The official death toll from the blazes stands at 12, but independent news outlets believe the figure to be much higher. Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the justice ministry to introduce the changes to the criminal law after more than 100 fires in the north-east of the country during an intense heatwave in northern Africa.

stories.title: RDC: une proposition de loi pour encadrer l'avortement déposée à l'Assemblée nationale
stories.summary: RDC: une proposition de loi pour encadrer l'avortement déposée à l'Assemblée nationale En République démocratique du Congo, le député national de la majorité Pacquis Nganini Atabakutuba a déposé une proposition de loi pour mieux encadrer l'interruption médicale de grossesse. Selon son auteur, il ne s'agit pas de légaliser l'avortement, mais d'harmoniser la loi congolaise avec le protocole de Maputo, signé par la RDC. Le texte doit encore franchir l'étape du bureau d'études de l'Assemblée nationale avant d'arriver devant les élus. Publié le : 01/10/2026 - 17:58 2 min Temps de lecture À l'Assemblée nationale de la RDC, une proposition de loi vise à harmoniser le droit congolais avec le protocole de Maputo sur l'avortement médicalisé. (Image d'illustration) © AFP Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Avec notre correspondante à Kinshasa , Paulina Zidi Pour l'auteur du texte, avocat de profession, il ne s'agit pas de légaliser l'avortement, mais d'harmoniser la loi congolaise avec le protocole de Maputo , signé par la RDC . Son article 14 impose aux États signataires de protéger les droits reproductifs des femmes, en autorisant l'avortement médicalisé dans des cas précis : agression sexuelle, viol, inceste, ainsi que certaines situations dans lesquelles la poursuite de la grossesse met gravement en danger la santé ou la vie de la mère ou du fœtus.

stories.title: Nigeria : comment des hommes politiques corrompus ont acheté "un bout d'Amérique"
stories.summary: Publicité Nigeria : comment des hommes politiques corrompus ont acheté "un bout d'Amérique" Afrique Un rapport publié par la plateforme de protection des lanceurs d'alerte en Afrique révèle avoir identifié près de 300 biens immobiliers aux États-Unis liés à des personnalités politiques nigérianes. Des propriétés acquises pour la plupart en liquide avec de l'argent public, alors que ces personnalités occupaient des fonctions officielles. La Californie fait partie des États où des biens immobiliers achetés par des personnalités politiques nigérianes ont été identifiés. © Michelle Mosqueda, Getty Images/AFP C'est un rapport qui lève une partie du voile sur l'ampleur de la corruption au Nigeria . La Plateforme de protection des lanceurs d'alerte en Afrique (PPLAAF) et l'Anti-Corruption Data Collective (ACDC) affirment dans ce document avoir identifié 284 propriétés immobilières aux États-Unis liées à 61 personnalités nigérianes qui occupent ou ont occupé des postes à responsabilité au sein de l'appareil d'État ou sécuritaire.

stories.title: Éliminatoires CAN 2027: démission de Carlos Queiroz, sélectionneur du Ghana
stories.summary: Éliminatoires CAN 2027: démission de Carlos Queiroz, sélectionneur du Ghana Un mois après avoir accepté de prolonger son mandat à la tête du Ghana malgré une première démission post-Mondial 2026, Carlos Queiroz a finalement quitté les Black Stars, sur fond de résultats décevants en qualifications pour la CAN 2027. Publié le : 01/10/2026 - 17:01 2 min Temps de lecture Carlos Quieroz lors de la Coupe du monde 2026, avec le Ghana. Carlos Queiroz a annoncé jeudi 1er octobre quitter son poste de sélectionneur de l’équipe de football du Ghana, cinq mois après sa prise de fonction et des résultats décevants. « Ce n’était pas une décision facile, mais les deux parties ont convenu que, dans les circonstances actuelles, mettre fin à notre relation professionnelle était la solution la plus appropriée, les intérêts du Ghana, des Black Stars et du football ghanéen primant sur tout le reste », a déclaré l’entraîneur portugais dans un message d’adieu publié sur le site web de la fédération jeudi. Il a ajouté que « les conditions nécessaires n’étaient pas pleinement réunies, et nos récentes performances ont contribué à la décision de mettre un terme à cette aventure ».

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Skips Independence Day Parade for Second Year Running
stories.summary: Nigeria: Coup - Tinubu's Govt Skips Independence Day Parade for Second Year Running SUNDAY AGHAEZE/Daily Trust PRESIDENT BUHARI ATTENDS NIGERIANâS 58TH INDEPENDENCE Nigerian Marking 58th Independence Anniversary with a parade (file photo) 1 October 2026 Daily Trust (Abuja) By Daily Trust For the second consecutive year, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's administration has dropped the traditional Independence Day military parade. The development has left unanswered questions over why the ceremony has not returned. This is despite the government's confirmation that officers accused of plotting a coup have been identified and are facing military trial. Unlike previous years when October 1 celebrations culminated in a ceremonial military parade, guard of honour, military drills and other displays of national pageantry, the Federal Government's official programme for Nigeria's 66th Independence anniversary contained no parade. stories.title: RDC: un membre de Médecins sans frontières infecté par Ebola évacué vers les Pays-Bas
stories.summary: RDC: un membre de Médecins sans frontières infecté par Ebola évacué vers les Pays-Bas Un membre du personnel de Médecins sans frontières (MSF) engagé dans la riposte contre Ebola en RDC a été évacué ce jeudi 1er octobre vers les Pays-Bas. stories.title: Cameroun: journée «ville morte» dans les régions anglophones, les forces de sécurité déployées
stories.summary: Cameroun: journée «ville morte» dans les régions anglophones, les forces de sécurité déployées Les séparatistes anglophones avaient appelé à une journée « ville morte » ce jeudi 1er octobre dans les régions anglophones du Cameroun, date anniversaire de la réunification du pays. stories.title: Au Kenya, le lancement en un temps record du chantier de la raffinerie Dangote
stories.summary: Le magnat nigérian Aliko Dangote ambitionne de répliquer sa raffinerie de Lagos à Lamu, une région isolée face à l’océan Indien. Mercredi 30 septembre, en présence de chefs d’Etat africains, s’est tenue une cérémonie hautement politique et symbolique.

stories.title: En RDC, Amnesty International lance une campagne pour lutter contre l'impunité
stories.summary: En RDC, Amnesty International lance une campagne pour lutter contre l'impunité En République démocratique du Congo, Amnesty International lance, jeudi 1er octobre, une campagne contre l'impunité, intitulée « Six millions de voix pour la justice au Congo ». Elle vise à sensibiliser le public, par le biais d'une pétition, mais aussi les responsables politiques, les diplomates et les représentants onusiens, afin de mettre en place des mécanismes judiciaires pour juger les exactions commises ces 30 dernières années, principalement dans l'est du pays. stories.title: Kenya: Politrack Poll - Ruto 45.1 Percent, Sifuna 19.6 Percent, Kalonzo 10.3 Percent If Elections Held Today
stories.summary: Kenya: Politrack Poll - Ruto 45.1 Percent, Sifuna 19.6 Percent, Kalonzo 10.3 Percent If Elections Held Today Capital FM President William Ruto (file photo) 1 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Correspondent Nairobi — President William Ruto leads the presidential preference survey by Politrack Africa, with 45.1 per cent of respondents saying they would vote for him if elections were held today. The survey, released at a press conference in Nairobi on Thursday, places Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna second at 19.6 per cent, followed by Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka at 10.3 per cent. stories.title: Kenya: Nairobi Tests Flood Response As Agencies Set Up Emergency Command Centre
stories.summary: Kenya: Nairobi Tests Flood Response As Agencies Set Up Emergency Command Centre Capitol FM Heavy rains left more than 23 people dead in Nairobi in March 2026. 1 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Correspondent Nairobi — Nairobi has begun testing its emergency response system ahead of the October-December rains, with national and county agencies setting up a joint command centre at Charter Hall. The exercise, dubbed Operation Okoa Maisha, is intended to test how authorities would respond to flooding and other emergencies, including the flow of information, deployment of rescue teams and evacuation of residents from high-risk areas. The exercise brings together the Nairobi County Government, National Disaster Operations Centre, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Defence Forces, Kenya Coast Guard and other emergency agencies. Charter Hall will serve as the central coordination point during the exercise, with participating agencies expected to relay reports from the field to a single command post. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Governor Johnson Sakaja said the arrangement was intended to avoid different agencies working with separate information during an emergency. "We need one report and one communication," Sakaja said.

stories.title: En Egypte, l’arrestation de six journalistes d’un média d’investigation, signe de la nervosité du régime du président Al-Sissi
stories.summary: Ce coup de force sans précédent arrive au moment où les autorités doivent faire face à un contexte économique tendu et à des rivalités politiques qui s’aiguisent pour succéder au président Abdel Fattah Al-Sissi, au pouvoir depuis 2013.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Compares His Tough Policies to Painful Cancer Treatment
stories.summary: Nigeria: Updated - Independence Anniversary: Tinubu Compares His Tough Policies to Painful Cancer Treatment Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu PrÃ©sident nigÃ©rian Bola Ahmed Tinubu 1 October 2026 Premium Times (Abuja) By Mariam Ileyemi "Nigeria was like a sick patient who receives the terrible news that he has cancer." President Bola Tinubu on Thursday compared his tough policies to the essential cancer treatment a patient needs. The Nigerian leader, in a televised address marking the country's 66th Independence Anniversary, said the situation inherited in 2023 warranted tough decisions that economists argue have caused Nigeria's worst cost of living crisis in a generation. "Nigeria was like a sick patient who receives the terrible news that he has cancer. His doctor explains that the treatment will be difficult and painful, but that it offers a strong prospect of recovery. He can begin treatment, endure its discomfort and fight the disease. Or he can ask only for morphine, dull the pain and leave the cancer to spread.

stories.title: Ethiopia: 'We Are Completely Isolated - Humanitarian Access Is Urgently Needed'
stories.summary: Ethiopia: Tigray, the Eparch of Adigrat Raises Alarm - 'We Are Completely Isolated - Humanitarian Access Is Urgently Needed' Alemnew Mekonnen/DW Alamata has changed hands several times (file photo). 1 October 2026 Fides News Agency (Vatican) Adigrat — "It is extremely urgent to facilitate humanitarian access, dialogue for peace and every form of dialogue. We are completely isolated, communications are blocked, and we have no contact with anyone." This is the message sent to Fides by the Eparch of Adigrat, Tesfaselassie Medhin, in a brief message sent with the support of UNICEF, which continues to assist the Church and, where possible, to maintain a minimum connection with the outside world. "All communications are blocked; our Church, our missions, religious, the local clergy, we are in our places, as usual," the Eparch said. "We will accompany and help the people with our presence, through which we carry out the Church's mission of incarnation." Medhin describes a situation of mounting difficulty: "Banks are also closed. We do not know for sure how our seminaries and schools will continue operating, but it is our intention to continue. We have no idea how we will manage provisions. Only God knows; we rely on Divine Providence." Meanwhile, the situation in Ethiopia's northern region continues to deteriorate (see Fides, 30/9/2026).

stories.title: Mass funeral held in Gaza City after 105 bodies recovered from rubble
stories.summary: Hundreds of mourners in Gaza City held a vigil on Wednesday for 105 people killed during Israel's war on the Palestinian territory. Their bodies were recovered in the past several days, after remaining buried under the rubble for nearly three years.

stories.title: Zimbabwe tycoon Wicknell Chivayo and wife killed in helicopter crash
stories.summary: Image source, Wicknell Chivayo/Instagram Image caption, Wicknell Chivayo was a prominent businessman known for his extravagant lifestyle By Wycliffe Muia Published 1 October 2026 Prominent Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife have been killed in a helicopter crash that left six people dead, his family have confirmed. The helicopter came down in the Marondera rural area, about 70km (43 miles) east of the capital, Harare, on Wednesday evening. Police said all six people on board died. Family spokesperson Herbert Chivayo confirmed the deaths of the 43-year-old businessman and his wife Lucy Muteke to state broadcaster ZBC, saying the family was devastated by the tragedy. Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to some African presidents and lucrative government contracts that had repeatedly attracted scrutiny.

stories.title: RDC : Denise Dusauchoy, itinéraire d’une influenceuse sous influence

stories.summary: Après avoir fait de l’offshore ivoirien sa porte d’entrée sur le continent en attendant d’étendre ses opérations au Maroc et au Cameroun via de nouveaux permis, Murphy Oil fait déjà face à un premier test décisif proposé par Abidjan.

stories.title: ‘They raped our country’: documentary follows Kenyans’ fight for restitution over stolen land
stories.summary: Much of the land taken during the colonial era has remained with the political elite and foreign companies occupying huge tea plantations. Photograph: Andrew H Brown View image in fullscreen Much of the land taken during the colonial era has remained with the political elite and foreign companies occupying huge tea plantations. Photograph: Andrew H Brown ‘They raped our country’: documentary follows Kenyans’ fight for restitution over stolen land Multinational tea companies still occupy ancestral highlands of communities displaced during British colonial era F or British colonialists, the fertile and cool uplands of central Kenya were the “White Highlands”, to be reserved exclusively for European settlers. Local communities were forced from the land, which was turned into plantations for tea and other crops. In recent decades, descendants of the displaced have fought to reclaim their ancestral land, some of which is now occupied by multinational tea companies and other large corporations.

stories.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5NX1O Prospective migrants who arrived in Greece are taken into a migration hub Image: Sofia Kleftaki/DW Advertisement Deportation centers are legally contentious, expensive and the subject of political controversy: For years, Brussels has been grappling with the issue of establishing such centers outside the EU for rejected asylum seekers. Previous attempts have failed due to legal objections, but now, a "group of five" consisting of Greece , Germany , Austria , Denmark and the Netherlands believes it has overcome these hurdles . During an interview with the Greek television channel ANT1, Greece's Minister of Migration, Thanos Plevris, stated that the first of these so-called " return hubs " is scheduled to begin operations as early as the second half of 2027 — just in time for Greece to assume the EU Council Presidency. Plevris said Greece had chosen an African country but could not reveal its name yet. Diplomatic circles and media outlets close to the EU have repeatedly cited Rwanda or Uganda , but neither country has been confirmed as the location.

Around 2,700 young athletes are expected to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports, with many qualifying through the African Youth Games last year. In 2025, the first major road cycling event took place on the continent, and in September this year it was announced the first-ever World Athletics Championships would be held in Kenya in 2029. There are also on-going negotiations about Formula 1 returning.

stories.title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Botswana is home to the world's largest elephant population, with more than 130,000 elephants (file photo) By Wycliffe Muia Published 30 September 2026 Animal rights activists have criticised Botswana's decision to authorise the killing of 23 elephants to provide meat for independence celebrations. The southern African country, home to the world's largest elephant population, is holding nationwide festivities on Wednesday to mark the 60th anniversary of independence from Britain. A licence issued by the Ministry of Environment and Tourism, seen by local media, authorises the hunting of 23 elephants and other wild animals for "complimentary purposes". The Botswana-based Elephant Protection Society warns the decision could undermine conservation, with its chairman Oaitse Nawa telling the BBC elephants needed greater protection. He warned that slaughtering elephants for celebratory feasting could encourage poaching by creating the impression that killing elephants is acceptable when sanctioned by government. "Elephants have lost their social structures because they are always being pushed from one place to another by gunshots," Nawa said.

stories.summary: Can she shape her own future? … Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud as Al-Sit and Mihad Murtada as Nafisa in Cotton Queen. Photograph: Frida Marzouk View image in fullscreen Can she shape her own future? … Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud as Al-Sit and Mihad Murtada as Nafisa in Cotton Queen. Photograph: Frida Marzouk Review Cotton Queen review – mystery, matriarchs and magic in pioneering Sudanese debut Suzannah Mirghani’s first feature contains a powerful performance by Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud as a village’s elder woman and tackles the long shadow of British imperialism and women’s rights ‘I decide my past,” says a village matriarch in this intriguingly political and poetic drama from Suzannah Mirghani, making her feature debut – and with it becoming the first Sudanese woman to direct a feature. (She was forced to cancel the original shoot in Sudan when war broke out in 2023 , moving production to Egypt.) It’s a film with things to say about the long shadow of the British empire, neocolonialism, women’s rights and female genital mutilation. But it mostly says it all without undermining its sense of mystery and shivers of magic realism. We’re in present day Sudan , where village elder Al-Sit (Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud) is an iron-willed woman not to be messed with.

Puntland Deputy Information Minister Bile Qabowsade said the five were killed by pirates before regional forces boarded MT Hoarner 25. He said the dead included three Pakistani nationals, one Indian and one national of Myanmar. Four other crew members were injured, including three Pakistanis and one Indian. stories.title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute
stories.summary: Image source, Ngabo Amon/BBC By Basillioh Rukanga Â and Â Bella Twine ,Â BBC Focus on Africa Published 29 September 2026 Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has been crowned king of Uganda's Tooro kingdom. The new monarch has long been a familiar face in the East African nation, where for many he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller: a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster. But the 56-year-old - now King Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I - has become the subject of media attention himself as his rise to the Tooro throne sparked controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country. Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms. For the last 31 years, it had been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.

stories.title: Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July. Here's what we know so far
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, The discovery of 12 bodies in an area east of Johannesburg has sparked alarm in South Africa By Khanyisile Ngcobo Reporting from Johannesburg Published 28 September 2026 Police in South Africa have confirmed the discovery of the bodies of three more women in an area east of Johannesburg, bringing the total number of bodies found there to 12 in just two months. The latest bodies were found in Ekurhuleni between Saturday and Monday morning, according to local police. Police have made arrests in three of the cases, which do not appear to be related to the others. Nevertheless, police have said they cannot rule out the possibility of a serial killer. The discoveries have caused widespread alarm in Ekurhuleni, particularly around Kempton Park, and come against the backdrop of longstanding concerns about high levels of violence against women in South Africa.

stories.title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Health workers at an Ebola treatment centre in Butembo, where mistrust of the response to the outbreak has fuelled a series of attacks. Photograph: Gradel Muyisa Mumbere/Reuters View image in fullscreen Health workers at an Ebola treatment centre in Butembo, where mistrust of the response to the outbreak has fuelled a series of attacks. Photograph: Gradel Muyisa Mumbere/Reuters DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak, a party representative has said. Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported. The party ‌said the attackers beat Karondwa, stole his belongings and set his house on fire, and that he later died from his injuries.

stories.title: Why are Ethiopia's rebels joining forces?
stories.summary: Why are Ethiopia's rebels joining forces? Why are Ethiopia's rebels joining forces? Close Seven rebel groups from across Ethiopia have announced a new alliance against Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. Some were once rivals, others fought separately, but they now say they're united by a common goal. So, who are they, and why have they joined forces now, just as fighting has flared once more in the northern Tigray region?

stories.title: Banished: the secret Trump deals sending migrants across the world - podcast
stories.summary: 00:00:00 00:00:00 Banished: the secret Trump deals sending migrants across the world - podcast Investigations correspondent Louisa Loveluck reports on the Trump administration’s secret deportation deals, sending thousands of migrants to ‘third countries’ across the world A Sierra Leonean nurse detained, handcuffed and flown to Ghana. An Iranian dissident to Central African Republic . A Cameroonian to Equatorial Guinea. This is the face of the Trump administration’s deportations policy since 2025 – striking deals with 35 countries, and sending up to 25,000 migrants in the US across the world, often to places they have no connection to at all. The Guardian investigations correspondent Louisa Loveluck – as part of a consortium of journalists organised by Forbidden Stories – uncovers some of the human stories behind these deals.

stories.title: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say
stories.summary: People gather at the store in Lwandle, near Cape Town, where 10 people were killed. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters View image in fullscreen People gather at the store in Lwandle, near Cape Town, where 10 people were killed. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say Seventeen people killed near Johannesburg in suspected ‘illegal goldmining turf war’, as 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police. The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.

stories.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys
stories.summary: The baboons’ presence has affected house prices on the Cape Peninsula, as they raid bins and kitchens and poo on properties. Photograph: Nic Bothma/Reuters View image in fullscreen The baboons’ presence has affected house prices on the Cape Peninsula, as they raid bins and kitchens and poo on properties. Photograph: Nic Bothma/Reuters ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents . The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.

stories.title: I have seen with pride how British overseas aid saves children’s lives. That is why I say cuts should be reversed | David Harewood
stories.summary: ‘UK funding for Sierra Leone’s newborn care programme is now expected to end in December 2026, two years earlier than planned.’ Photograph: Jonathan Porter/Alamy View image in fullscreen ‘UK funding for Sierra Leone’s newborn care programme is now expected to end in December 2026, two years earlier than planned.’ Photograph: Jonathan Porter/Alamy I have seen with pride how British overseas aid saves children’s lives. That is why I say cuts should be reversed David Harewood I understand the pressure on the public purse, but I have also seen the effect of our spending on the ground. Our choices can do so much good David Harewood is a Unicef UK ambassador A s Labour party conference approaches, politicians will debate spending priorities, fiscal pressures and the UK’s place in the world. Before those discussions begin, I want ministers to picture a hospital ward I visited in Sierra Leone with Unicef (United Nations Children’s Fund). Inside the special-care baby unit at Makeni regional hospital were rows of tiny premature babies, some no bigger than my hand.

stories.title: South African white genocide does not exist, new ambassador to US tells BBC
stories.summary: Figure caption, Are claims of a white genocide in South Africa real? By Ione Wells ,Â in Washington ,Â Mayeni Jones ,Â in Johannesburg Â and Â Ed Habershon ,Â in Johannesburg Published 26 September 2026 South Africa's new ambassador to Washington has a personal reason to challenge Donald Trump's assertion that there is a genocide against white Afrikaners - he is "a born Afrikaner" himself. "Is he talking about us?" Roelf Meyer remembers thinking when he first heard the US president say it. His response to Trump's claim is blunt. The notion of a mass attack on the white Afrikaner minority in South Africa does not exist, he told the BBC, adding that his identity gave him the legitimacy to say so. Meyer was one of the chief mediators to end white-minority rule, known as apartheid, in South Africa in the 1990s.
